name: MIPLIB 2017 open instance cdc7-4-3-2
description: Find a feasible solution of the MIPLIB 2017 instance cdc7-4-3-2 with as low an objective value as possible (a maximisation model is negated, so that lower is better for every instance). A solution is feasible when every variable bound, every row bound and the integrality of every integer variable hold within an absolute tolerance of 1e-6 on the values as they are returned; integer variables are not rounded first.

sources.locator: A subspace code of size $333$ in the setting of a binary $q$-analog of the Fano plane
Gleixner et al. (2021), MIPLIB 2017: data-driven compilation of the 6th mixed-integer programming library (benchmark paper, not evidence).
Instance pages with submitter, group, status and best known objective.

execution.interface: solve(model) -> numpy array of num_cols values, one per column. model has name, mps_path (the uncompressed MPS file), num_cols, num_rows, A (scipy CSR matrix of the rows), col_cost, col_lower, col_upper, row_lower, row_upper, integrality (bool array), offset, maximise and indicators (a list of (row, column, value): such a row has to hold only when that column equals the value; empty for most instances). Score: col_cost @ x + offset in minimisation form (negated when maximise is true), minimized; an infeasible vector is invalid.

limitations: The objective listed on the open-instances page may have been improved since 2026-11-11 (the list did not change between 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-11).
Candidates may call HiGHS through highspy; a stronger solver is a method, not a discovery by the workflow.
The record was reproduced by this task's verifier from a published solution (or an optimiser run). See VALIDITY.md.

checks: the published solution, checked by our verifier: feasible within 1e-6, objective -333.0

science_relevance.reason: The paper has the construction of large binary subspace codes with these parameters (A_2(7,4;3)) as its main objective, and the task asks for a code of this size from the MIPLIB model.
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Find a maximum set of 3-dimensional subspaces of GF(2)^7 whose pairwise intersections have dimension at most 1 (a constant-dimension code with parameters n=7, d=4, k=3, q=2), in the integer programming model cdc7-4-3-2.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Subspace codes are used in random network coding; A_2(7,4;3) is only known to lie between 333 and 381, and a code of size 381 would be a binary q-analog of the Fano plane, whose existence is a well known open question.

papers.title: A subspace code of size $333$ in the setting of a binary $q$-analog of the Fano plane
papers.task_relation: The task is the integer programming (clique) model of the same code problem; a feasible solution larger than 333 would improve the bound reported in the paper.
papers.primary_goal: Construct a binary constant-dimension subspace code of length 7, dimension 3 and minimum distance 4 with 333 words, improving the previous lower bound of 329.
